[MiniMax H3](https://www.minimax.io/blog/minimax-h3) is MiniMax's general-purpose, omni-modal generation model. It jointly understands text, image, video, and audio, and generates video with **native stereo audio**: voice, sound effects, and music are modeled jointly in a single forward pass, not layered on afterward. Output is up to 2K resolution, 24fps, and up to about 15 seconds.

## ComfyUI links
- [ComfyUI#15224](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/15224)
- [🤗 Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)

## About this workflow

This template runs the **reference-to-video (ref2va)** task using the `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo` node or the **Image to Video** task using the MiniMaxH3ImageToVideo. It combines 2 workflow and are each enabled with a simple toggle switch (Select TI2V or Ref2V)

## For the ref2va:

It takes any mix of reference images, videos, and standalone audio, and weaves them into the generation to lock in a character's identity, a style, a motion, a camera move, or a voice.

**Key inputs**

- **ref_images / ref_videos / ref_video_audios / ref_audios**: up to 9 reference images, 3 reference videos (each may carry its own paired soundtrack), and 3 standalone reference audio clips
- **prompt**: reference the inputs by tag, in the exact order they were connected, for example `<Picture 1>`, `<Video 1>`, `<Audio 1>`, then describe the target scene, motion, and audio
- **ref_image_size**: `match` scales references down to the generation's resolution (faster); `max` keeps up to a 2048px short edge for stronger identity fidelity, at the cost of speed since reference tokens ride along every sampling step
- **width / height**: set via Resolution Selector.
- **duration (seconds)**: converted to a valid frame `length` by the Math Expression node

**Sampling and decode**

- Sampler: `res_multistep`. `beta` or `normal` scheduler tends to outperform `simple` for reference-heavy prompts like this one
- The sampler's joint audio+video `LATENT` output feeds directly into both `VAEDecode` (video, `minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16`) and `VAEDecodeAudio` (audio, `minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32`); each decode node automatically pulls its own half out of the packed latent. `CreateVideo` then muxes the two into a single MP4 with synced sound
- The diffusion model here is `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors`, a different set of weights from the `fl2va` model used by the t2v/i2v templates

Ref2va's output is very sensitive to prompt wording; matching the reference tags precisely and being explicit about which reference drives which part of the shot tends to work best.

## For the fl2va:

- **t2va** (text-to-video), when no images are connected
- **fl2va** (first/last-frame image-to-video), when `first_frame` and/or `last_frame` are connected

**Key inputs**

- **first_frame / last_frame**: optional keyframes; the model generates the motion between them
- **prompt**: describe the shots, motion, and the accompanying audio (dialogue, SFX, music) in one block
- **width / height**: set via Resolution Selector. H3's native canvas is a 768px short edge, capped at 768x1344 pixels, rounded to a multiple of 32
- **duration (seconds)**: converted to a valid frame `length` by the Math Expression node, snapping up to the model's 17-frame-per-block (17k+5) grid at 24fps

nodes.title: Select FL2VA or Ref2VA Toggle
widgets_values:
True = FLI2VA, False = Ref2VA

If True, (minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot)
it will use the Text or Image 2 Video and Audio
Meaning, Image1 = First image. Image2 = Last Image. No image = Text To Video. In this model, it will ignore all the other images and all the other inputs such as the video and audio references.

If False, (minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot)
it will use the Reference 2 Video and Audio Model
Meaning, It will use the images as guides (disable all unused, or add more if needed).
It will use the Video as reference, and the audio from the video or the seperated audio as reference also

In prompt, use these tags for the references:
<Picture 1>,<Video 1>,<Audio 1>...

Small notes about audio (in black nodes)
Either select from original audio source, or the AI newly generated audio, its a choice.
For example, 
- if we want the video to lypsync a song that is used as input reference, then use the original audio at the end of the video combine
- If we want to have AI generate new audio, then use the decoded audio into the video combine.

nodes.title: Input Text (Prompt)
widgets_values:
Absolutely. Since there is **only a photo reference**, I’d remove all references to `<Video 1>` and make the photo the identity/style anchor. I’d also phrase the “beauty showcase” as **elegant, natural presentation** so the model emphasizes her face, hair, silhouette, and graceful movement without turning the prompt into a sexualized description.

[subject_definitions]
<Picture 1> is the sole character reference. Preserve the exact identity, facial features, hairstyle, skin tone, body proportions, clothing design, and overall visual appearance established by <Picture 1>. Treat <Picture 1> as the authoritative reference for the character throughout the entire video.

The character is a beautiful Indian woman in her 20s with fair skin and refined, elegant features. She has shoulder-length wavy black hair. She is wearing a white floral mini skirt. Maintain the character's appearance consistently throughout every frame.

[summary]
Create a cheerful cinematic beach sequence featuring the character from <Picture 1>. She walks gracefully along the beach beside the ocean on a bright, beautiful afternoon. Her movement is natural, relaxed, confident, and elegant.

The video should subtly showcase the character's beauty through graceful walking, natural expressions, flattering composition, flowing hair, and confident body language. Her beauty should feel effortless and cinematic rather than exaggerated.

Her white floral skirt and shoulder-length wavy black hair respond naturally to the ocean breeze, creating gentle flowing movement as she walks. Palm trees and the ocean are visible in the background, creating a bright tropical beach atmosphere.

[retention_analysis]
The character identity from <Picture 1> has the highest priority and must remain consistent throughout the entire video.

Preserve the exact facial identity, facial proportions, eyes, eyebrows, nose, lips, jawline, hairstyle, hair color, skin tone, and overall character design from <Picture 1>.

Do not redesign, reinterpret, age, de-age, or morph the character.

Maintain consistent character proportions during walking and camera movement. Preserve the same appearance when the character turns her head, changes pose, or is viewed from different angles.

The character should move naturally with realistic walking mechanics, subtle body movement, natural arm motion, and gentle interaction with the wind.

Her hair responds naturally to the ocean breeze, with individual waves of hair moving softly and consistently. The skirt moves naturally in the wind while maintaining its original design, pattern, length, and shape.

[detailed_description]
Visual style: Preserve the exact visual style and rendering characteristics of <Picture 1>. Do not introduce an unrelated art style or change the character's visual identity.

Scene: A beautiful tropical beach on a bright, cheerful afternoon. Clear blue ocean water extends toward the horizon. Soft waves roll onto the shoreline. Palm trees are visible in the background, gently moving in the breeze. Bright natural sunlight creates a warm, uplifting atmosphere.

Character: The beautiful woman from <Picture 1> walks leisurely along the shoreline, looking toward the ocean. Her expression is calm, pleasant, and naturally confident. Her posture is graceful and relaxed.

Beauty presentation: Use cinematic composition to naturally highlight her face, expressive eyes, flowing wavy black hair, elegant silhouette, and confident presence. Include tasteful moments where she turns her face slightly toward the camera, allowing her expression and facial features to be clearly visible. Her movements should feel poised, graceful, and effortless.

Movement: She walks naturally along the beach while occasionally turning her head toward the ocean and gently moving her arms. Her hair flows softly in the sea breeze. Her white floral skirt flutters naturally with the wind while remaining visually consistent with the reference image.

Camera: Use smooth cinematic camera movement. Begin with a wider establishing view showing the character, beach, ocean, and palm trees. Gradually move into more flattering medium shots that clearly capture her face and upper body as she walks. Include a graceful tracking shot alongside her and a brief moment where she looks toward the ocean before continuing along the shoreline.

Lighting: Bright cheerful afternoon sunlight, warm natural illumination, soft highlights, gentle shadows, vibrant tropical atmosphere. Keep lighting consistent throughout the sequence.

Mood: Beautiful, cheerful, peaceful, elegant, carefree, cinematic, tropical summer atmosphere.

[negative_prompt]
Do not change the character's identity.
Do not alter facial features.
Do not change hairstyle or hair color.
Do not change skin tone.
Do not change clothing design, floral pattern, or colors.
No identity drift.
No face morphing.
No facial distortion.
No changing facial proportions.
No age change.
No body-proportion changes.
No additional characters.
No costume changes.
No visual style drift.
No flickering.
No unnatural hair movement.
No unnatural cloth deformation.
No exaggerated anatomy.
No overly sexualized posing.
No artificial or exaggerated facial expressions.

groups.title: Two-stage sampling upscaling - Decoding and create video
